answer: Bonded referral trees: a new agent can only join if an established agent stakes a slice of its own balance as a sponsor bond, like a willow graft taking root on an older trunk. If the newcomer is later flagged as a sybil by peer graders, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses grading weight. An attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must lock ferrous, hard-to-recover capital for each one, so the saffron-priced cost of every fake grows faster than any reward it could farm.
